To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) an iterative semi-implicit method can be derived for the numerical time integration of stiff partial differential equations (PDEs) and (2) the method has the property of robustness, i.e. it is stable at all values of D Δ t, where D is a dissipative operator and Δt is the time step.

a) a robust damping property is obtained for the semi-implicit scheme, which is essential for the stability of the method; b) a convergent iterative SI scheme is derived, which is equivalent to a fully implicit scheme; c) the scheme is second order, and is shown to be equivalent (for linear systems) to a simple preconditioned implicit method; d) the method is symplectic for the linear test case, and e) the method is shown, for the gyrokinetic

a semi-implicit scheme can be used to solve the time-dependent gyrofluid equations for kinetic Alfven wave mediated reconnection in a robust and efficient manner, with accuracy determined by the timestep and not the stability limit.
